title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is folio 2 of a short set of notes, pp. 113–115, that sets up an explicit combinatorial model of the fundamental groupoid of a punctured surface carrying a dessin/map. The motivation is the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower. Page 113 fixed the following data:
- X is a (possibly non-orientable) map, R its set of flags ('repères') r=(s,a,f), and S=S_0⊔S_1⊔S_∞ its vertices, edges and faces, each realized by a point R_φ.
- Each flag r is a triangle of the barycentric subdivision, with corners R_s, R_a, R_f of types 0, 1, ∞.
- The cartographic group acts by the involutions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞, with (τ_0τ_∞)^2=1. The rotations are ρ_∞=τ_1τ_0, ρ_0=τ_∞τ_1, ρ_1=τ_0τ_∞, and ρ_∞ρ_1ρ_0=1.

This page:
(6) For each flag r and each ordered pair (i,j) of distinct types, he introduces a point R_r^{i,j}. It lies near the corner of type i of the triangle r, on the side of r joining the corners of types i and j. The margin identifies {0,1,∞} with Z/3, so i+1 and i+2 make sense.
(7) The only relations among these points are R_r^{i,j}=R_{τ_k(r)}^{i,j} for k∉{i,j}. The side ij of r is shared with the adjacent flag τ_k(r), the one opposite the corner of type k. Hence there are 6|R|/2 = 3|R| distinct points.
(8) λ_r^i : R_r^{i,i+1} → R_r^{i,i+2} is the small arc turning around the corner of type i inside r, in the sense of the orientation of r.
(9) a_r^i is the arc running along the side of r opposite the corner of type i, joining the two points near the other two corners. These arcs circle the flag-triangle as a closed contour in the sense of its orientation d_r.
(10) The only identifications are a_r^i = a_{τ_i(r)}^i: the side is shared with τ_i(r). There are no other identities and no redundancies.

The closing NB, which runs onto p.115, explains the geometric meaning:
- The combinatorial map has its canonical conformal realization, a Riemann surface X with Belyi map to P^1 branched over 0, 1, ∞.
- One takes the real oriented blow-up of X at all the points R_φ (φ∈S). This gives a real-analytic, non-conformal surface with boundary, denoted X̃^{***}, whose interior is X∖S.
- The R_r^{ij} are points on the boundary circles, i.e. tangential directions at R_φ. The λ are arcs on the boundary circles; the a are arcs along the sides of the barycentric triangles.

On p.115 the hexagon relation (12), one per flag (the boundary of the truncated triangle is trivial), completes a presentation of the fundamental groupoid π_1(X̃^{**}, {R_r^{ij}}). This amounts to a fundamental groupoid with tangential base points, six per flag, adapted to the dessin. The marginal 'CAS ... degré = 1' presumably refers to the base case P^1 with the three points 0, 1, ∞.
errors: (7) is written with σ_k but must mean the adjacency involutions τ_k of p.113; with τ_k the relation is geometrically correct.

The source and target in (9) are partly crossed out and hard to read. The consistent reading, forced by (10) and by (12) on p.115, is that a_r^i joins the two points on the side opposite corner i (R_r^{i+1,i+2} and R_r^{i+2,i+1}, in the direction of the orientation d_r). The transcribed 'R_r^{i+1,i} → R_r^{i+1,i+2}' would instead describe a corner arc, duplicating λ.

Euler characteristic check succeeds, so the presentation is consistent: 3|R| points, 3|R|+3|R|/2 arcs and |R| hexagonal cells give χ=-|R|/2. This equals χ(X)-|S|, where χ(X)=|S|-|R|/2 from the barycentric subdivision.
Composition order and directions in (12) on p.115 are ambiguous as transcribed. This does not affect the structure: one hexagon relation per flag.

ideas.what: Base points R_r^{ij} attached to each corner and side of each flag, i.e. points on the boundary circles of the real oriented blow-up at vertices, edge-midpoints and face-centres.
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points adapted to a dessin d'enfant
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points') for tangential base points; Ihara and Nakamura for their use in Galois actions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) stresses groupoids with well-chosen base points for the Teichmüller tower. Explicit tangential base points are not, to my knowledge, described there.

ideas.what: Combinatorial presentation of the fundamental groupoid of X∖S (blown up) from the flag/barycentric structure: corner arcs λ, side arcs a, identifications via the τ_k, and one hexagon relation per flag.
ideas.modern_name: van Kampen presentation of the fundamental groupoid from a cellular decomposition (truncated barycentric triangulation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Brown's groupoid van Kampen); dessin-adapted versions appear in Schneps, Lochak–Schneps, and Nakamura

ideas.what: Canonical conformal realization of a combinatorial map as a Riemann surface, with real oriented blow-up of the marked points to obtain a surface with boundary X̃^{***} and variants with only some types blown up.
ideas.modern_name: Belyi/dessin correspondence plus real oriented blow-up (Kato–Nakayama-type space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (dessins); real blow-up is classical (A'Campo, Kato–Nakayama for the log version)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (canonical conformal structure on maps); the blow-up detail is unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck, apparently before 1984, sets up explicit tangential base points: points on the boundary circles of the real oriented blow-up at the vertices, edge-centres and face-centres of a dessin. He indexes them by flags and ordered pairs of types, and gives a full groupoid presentation with these base points. This anticipates the tangential-base-point formalism of Deligne (1989), used by Ihara, Nakamura and Lochak–Schneps for Galois actions on Teichmüller groupoids.
missed.quote: on la note X̃^{***} ; ... Les points R_r^{ij} et les chemins précédents seront regardés ... comme points et chemins dans X̃^{**}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the 'many tangential base points' groupoid viewpoint for the Galois action on dessins and Teichmüller groupoids was worked out concretely by Grothendieck. The flag-indexed basepoint set, compatible with the cartographic group, is a natural choice not standardly presented in that form.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine van Kampen presentation. The historically notable point is the early, explicit use of boundary points of the real oriented blow-up as base points, indexed by flags of a dessin. In spirit this is tangential base points before Deligne, but the general idea is known and Grothendieck's influence on that circle is acknowledged.
transcription_corrections: (7): the image has σ_k(r), but this should be read as τ_k(r).
'R_r^{i de r} (=R_s, R_∞, R_φ suivant...)' should read 'sommet de type i de r (= R_s, R_a, R_f suivant que i=0,1,∞)'.
(9): the source superscript is crossed out and overwritten; geometrically it should be the point near corner i+2 on the side opposite i (R_r^{i+2,i+1}), not R_r^{i+1,i}.
'Rep{0,1,∞}' denotes ordered pairs (repères) of distinct elements of {0,1,∞}.

Final NB: 'réalisation conforme canonique, qui réalise par une surface analytique réelle ... on peut considérer son éclaté en les R_φ (φ∈S) ... qui est une surface à bord analytique réelle (mais pas conforme) dont l'intérieur s'identifie à X∖S, on la note'. Read 'éclaté' rather than 'relation/découpe de l'identité'.
The left margin begins 'NB On écrit pour simplifier i+1, i+2 au lieu des permutations circulaires (0,1,∞),(1,∞,0),(∞,0,1), i.e. on identifie {0,1,∞} à Z/3Z'.
